questions.question: What is Bundler and how does it manage gems?
questions.title: Bundler Basics
questions.direct_answer: Bundler is Ruby's dependency manager: it reads the Gemfile (the gems your app needs), resolves versions, and installs them with bundle install, writing Gemfile.lock (the exact resolved versions). You run your app with bundle exec ruby app.rb so it loads the exact gem versions from the lock, not whatever's on the system. Bundler solves 'it works on my machine' — the lock pins exact versions so every machine and prod runs the same gems. bundle update GEM bumps one gem; bundle update bumps all (re-resolves). You add a gem to the Gemfile, run bundle install, and the lock records the resolved versions.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know Bundler reads the Gemfile, installs with bundle install, writes Gemfile.lock, and runs with bundle exec to load exact versions.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Running without bundle exec (loads system gems, not the locked versions), or committing code without Gemfile.lock.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Bundler reads the Gemfile, installs with bundle install, writes Gemfile.lock (exact versions). Run with bundle exec to load those versions; solves 'works on my machine'.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Bundler is Ruby's dependency manager; it reads the Gemfile and resolves versions.
bundle install installs and writes Gemfile.lock (the exact resolved versions).
Run with bundle exec to load the locked versions, not system gems.
The lock solves 'it works on my machine' — every machine and prod uses the same gems.
Commit Gemfile AND Gemfile.lock together; bundle update to bump.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Bundler is Ruby's dependency manager: it reads the Gemfile — the gems your app needs — resolves versions, and installs them with bundle install, writing Gemfile.lock with the exact resolved versions. You run your app with bundle exec ruby app.rb so it loads the exact gem versions from the lock, not whatever's installed on the system. Bundler solves it works on my machine: the lock pins exact versions so every developer's machine and production run the same gems. bundle update GEM bumps one gem; bundle update bumps all by re-resolving. You add a gem to the Gemfile, run bundle install, and the lock records the resolved versions to commit alongside your code. A common mistake is running without bundle exec, which loads system gems, not the locked versions, and committing code without Gemfile.lock.

sections.title: Build the mental model
sections.content:
Bundler is Ruby's dependency manager: it reads the Gemfile (the gems your app needs), resolves versions, and installs them with bundle install, writing Gemfile.lock (the exact resolved versions).

You run your app with bundle exec ruby app.rb so it loads the exact gem versions from the lock, not whatever's on the system.

Bundler solves 'it works on my machine' — the lock pins exact versions so every machine and prod runs the same gems. bundle update GEM bumps one gem; bundle update bumps all (re-resolves). You add a gem to the Gemfile, run bundle install, and the lock records the resolved versions.

Running without bundle exec (loads system gems, not the locked versions), or committing code without Gemfile.lock.

sections.title: Gemfile -> lock -> bundle exec
sections.content:
The Gemfile lists gems; bundle install resolves and writes the lock; bundle exec loads those exact versions.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G[Gemfile] --> I[bundle install] --> L[Gemfile.lock]
  L --> X[bundle exec ruby app.rb]
```

sections.title: Bundler workflow
sections.content:
```ruby
# Gemfile (list the gems your app needs)
source 'https://rubygems.org'
gem 'rails', '~> 7.0'
gem 'pg'
gem 'sidekiq'

# Install gems (resolves versions, writes Gemfile.lock):
#   bundle install

# Run your app with the EXACT locked versions:
#   bundle exec ruby app.rb
#   bundle exec rails server
#   bundle exec rspec

# Bump ONE gem (re-resolve just it):
#   bundle update sidekiq
# Bump ALL gems (re-resolve everything):
#   bundle update

# Add a gem: put it in the Gemfile, then `bundle install` (updates the lock).
# Commit BOTH Gemfile and Gemfile.lock together.
```
